posts.author: Tom's Hardware
posts.text: AMD debuts Helion reference design for agentic AI servers with up to 32,768 Zen 6 ‘Venice’ cores. At the OCP Global Summit, AMD revealed Helion, a rack-scale reference design for agentic AI that can house up to 32,768 Zen 6 CPU cores.

posts.author: NVIDIA
posts.text: OCP Global Summit: Amid Ecosystem Adoption, NVIDIA Opens Vera Rubin Architecture to Help Scale AI Factories Worldwide. As AI factories grow from megawatts to gigawatts, building them takes more than advanced computing. Open standards are helping the industry scale AI infrastructure faster, more efficiently and more reliably. At the Open Compute Project (OCP) Global Summit, taking place in the San Jose McEnery Convention Center, NVIDIA announced new partnerships and contributions aimed at […]

posts.author: Bloomberg Tech
posts.text: Cisco, Nvidia Tackle AI’s Growing Data Center Bottleneck. Cisco is partnering with Nvidia on a new generation of optical networking technology designed to handle the exploding amount of data moving through AI data centers. Cisco President and Chief Product Officer Jeetu Patel explains why increasingly powerful AI agents could consume far more network bandwidth than humans performing the same tasks, and how faster, more power-efficient connections could help hundreds of thousands of GPUs operate together while lowering the cost of AI. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

posts.author: The Verge AI
posts.text: Microsoft’s new AI chip makes it less reliant on Nvidia’s GPUs. Microsoft is announcing its third-generation Maia in-house AI chip today, designed to be the "primary AI inference system" for Microsoft's products and services. Maia 300 not only improves the cost and efficiency of running AI workloads in the cloud, it's also more capable of handling the latest reasoning models and agentic tasks. Maia 300 will […]

posts.author: The Decoder
posts.text: Microsoft plans to scale its own Maia AI chips to gigawatt levels by 2027. Microsoft will make its in-house Azure Maia chips the main AI inference system across its products starting in 2027, deploying them at multi-gigawatt scale. The upcoming Maia 300 should deliver 40 percent more tokens per megawatt than leading GPU systems. CEO Satya Nadella calls it "our biggest bet yet on our own silicon." The article Microsoft plans to scale its own Maia AI chips to gigawatt levels by 2027 appeared first on The Decoder .

posts.author: Bloomberg Tech
posts.text: Microsoft Ramps Up Homegrown AI Chip Push. Microsoft is installing the latest version of its Maia chips in data centers to power its AI software using mostly homegrown hardware. The company expects to stock multiple gigawatts of its Maia chips, with the Maia 300 starting to roll out next year. Bloomberg's Matt Day joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

posts.author: Bloomberg Tech
posts.text: Microsoft, Musk Race to Reinvent the AI Chip. Bloomberg’s Ed Ludlow breaks down Microsoft's latest homegrown Maia chips, its latest effort to rely less on outside semiconductors to power its AI ambitions. Plus, Elon Musk wants to put chip development on fast-forward, testing as many as ten new designs a year; and Apple is finally ready to unveil its new smart home strategy, seeking to plug a major hole in its ecosystem. (Source: Bloomberg)

posts.author: The Decoder
posts.text: Google Deepmind's AlphaProof Nexus solved dozens of open math problems and actually got peer reviewed. Google Deepmind's AlphaProof Nexus solved dozens of open math problems, including nine Erdős problems two of which were unsolved for 56 years, per a study in Science. The publication comes as OpenAI faces a boycott for dumping AI proofs on GitHub without peer review. Deepmind had its results reviewed before publishing. The article Google Deepmind's AlphaProof Nexus solved dozens of open math problems and actually got peer reviewed appeared first on The Decoder .

posts.author: The Decoder
posts.text: Anthropic's Andrej Karpathy says "the external world has seen the preview" of what AI can actually do. Andrej Karpathy, co-founder of OpenAI and now at Anthropic, sees a widening knowledge gap in AI. About 75 percent of the world's population has barely touched LLMs. Roughly 5,000 people, meanwhile, have access to internal frontier systems whose agent swarms do work that would take top experts years. The public, at best, sees a weird chatbot. The article Anthropic's Andrej Karpathy says "the external world has seen the preview" of what AI can actually do appeared first on The Decoder .

posts.author: The Decoder
posts.text: White House reverses course and restores UK AI Safety Institute's access to frontier models. The White House has reversed course and restored the UK's AI Security Institute's early access to AI models from Anthropic, Google DeepMind, and OpenAI. In September, the Trump administration had told the companies to stop sharing their models with the British agency. Diplomatic pressure from AI Minister Kanishka Narayan led to the reversal. The article White House reverses course and restores UK AI Safety Institute's access to frontier models appeared first on The Decoder .

posts.author: Bloomberg Tech
posts.text: How the OpenAI, Anthropic IPOs Could Lift the Veil on AI Economics. VistaShares portfolio manager and DVX Ventures principal David Fetherstonhaugh says investors are increasingly looking for proof that massive AI spending is generating returns. He discusses why private companies like OpenAI and Anthropic leave a key part of the AI economy opaque and how their eventual IPOs could bring greater transparency to the ecosystem. He joins Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

posts.text: Meta's new frontier model Muse Wonder Full breaks into the AI top tier. Meta's new Muse Wonder models rank in the top three on six out of ten benchmarks, with the biggest gains in agentic tasks. But the cost per task has nearly tripled. posts.author: Bloomberg Tech
posts.text: Anthropic AI Model Goes Rogue, Gives Cops a Fake Tip. Anthropic PBC said its Claude AI model went rogue and carried out unintended actions on the digital systems of outside organizations. In one example, the AI model gave police in Philadelphia a fake tip on a homicide case. The police took no action. Other unintended behaviors were also noted. Bloomberg's Ed Ludlow reports. (Source: Bloomberg)
